## CEO BRIEFING

**To:** Dana Whitfield · **From:** Incident Commander · **14:20 UTC, Mon 9 Nov 2026** · Incident INC-2026-1109-01

**Bottom line.** Batch API incident. Open but mitigated — not resolved, not root-caused. Impact ran 11:42–12:58 UTC (76 minutes). Our verification window closes at 14:30, 30 minutes before your board call; if it closes clean we can declare the incident resolved then, but root cause will still be open and one worker fleet is still out of rotation.

**Impact — the headline figure.** 17,602 failed Batch API requests out of 58,900 Batch API requests in the window — **29.9%**. For context, Northstar served 842,000 requests across all surfaces in the same window; the Batch API is about 7% of that. Only the Batch API was affected: Inference, Embeddings and Files are fine. Use the 29.9% figure; do not break impact down by worker fleet — that is internal deployment detail and not a reporting basis.

Seven of our 36 accounts took failures: stark-industries, contoso, wayne-enterprises, globex, wonka-industries, umbrella-health, initech.

**What we don't know — and this is the important part.** Root cause. Two candidates, both live, neither tested:

- **H1 (leading):** release `r3`, shipped 11:31, cut the batch worker database connection pool from 80 to 24 per worker. Timing fits and workers were queueing on DB connections. But `r3` went to both fleets and only one degraded — so on its own it does not explain the incident.
- **H2:** concentrated load, about 3x normal, driven by one large scheduled job.
- **H3 (rejected):** the upstream object-storage provider — status green, and the Files API on the same provider stayed healthy throughout.

We deliberately did **not** roll `r3` back at 12:31: rolling back would destroy the evidence needed to test H1. We moved traffic instead.

**Still open.** Verification window (closes 14:30); `r3` rollback test not run; the affected fleet drained and out of rotation; re-drive of failed jobs ~60% complete with no failures so far.

**What you can say if it comes up.** Only these lines, which are the whole of what comms has cleared:

- there is an incident affecting the Batch API, and it started at 11:42 UTC;
- a mitigation has been applied and the service is recovering;
- we are monitoring before we confirm recovery;
- a further update will follow, with a stated time.

To any named customer, their own figures only. Please don't speculate on cause, and don't give a completion time — engineering's internal wrap-up estimate is not for use outside the incident channel.

**Contoso.** Our most exposed account and the one to watch commercially: 9,400 Batch requests, 3,410 failures in the window. They have written twice, the second time asking directly about Schedule B service credits. We have told them B.5 determines Monthly Availability after month end and publishes it within 10 business days, with 30 days to claim from publication — so we cannot confirm a breach or a credit now, and haven't. One internal flag for later: Contoso's retry-without-backoff behaviour was flagged on 4 Nov (TKT-8841) and their fix is still behind their Q4 freeze; that may bear on the credit calculation under B.2(b). Not a position to take publicly, or to them, yet.

**Comms status.** The 12:05 status page update said we had "identified" the cause. That was wrong; Marcus stopped all cause statements at 12:09. A corrected update goes out now. One approval gap: we cannot yet tell customers whether failed jobs will be replayed — wonka has already asked — because the re-drive is not on the cleared list.

**Separate, not part of this incident:** Marcus raised SEC-411 (batch worker database role holds write access to the billing schema). No link to this incident, no contributing factor, already ticketed and owned by Marcus for this week. Staff-only — not for the board call.

---

## ENGINEERING UPDATE

**INC-2026-1109-01 — Batch API — IC handover, 14:20 UTC.** Incident OPEN: mitigated, verification in progress, root cause not established.

**State**
- 12:58: all Batch API traffic cut over to fleet-b; fleet-a drained and held out of rotation.
- Error rate on `POST /v1/batch/jobs`: 0.3% and holding. Baseline 0.2%. fleet-b queue depth normal.
- Verification window opened 13:00, closes **14:30**. Policy requires 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate. Nothing is declared resolved before that closes clean.
- Re-drive of jobs that failed in the window: ~60% complete at 13:52, no failures on re-drive.

**Open / not established**
- Root cause. **H1** connection-pool change in `r3` (max pool 80→24 per worker, shipped 11:31) — leading, untested, and does not explain why fleet-b on the same release stayed clean. **H2** concentrated load on fleet-a (~3x from 11:38, one large wonka scheduled job) — live, untested. They may interact; that is a third untested proposition. **H3** upstream storage rejected at 11:47.
- `r3` rollback test not run. Decision at 12:31: do not roll back; keep fleet-a's state as the evidence, mitigate by moving traffic instead.
- fleet-a not returned to service.

**Next**
1. **14:30** — if the window closes clean, declare resolved.
2. Run the `r3` rollback test on the isolated fleet-a. This is the discriminating experiment for H1 vs H2 and the top priority once the window closes.
3. Decide fleet-a's return to rotation on the back of that test.
4. Finish the re-drive.
5. Watch fleet-b — it is now carrying the entire Batch workload on its own.

**Watch-outs**
- Do not use "fixed", "resolved" or "root cause identified". We have already had one premature "identified", on the 12:05 status page.
- Nothing about cause goes external until Marcus confirms it. Ruth publishes only from Tomas' cleared list.
- Keep SEC-411 out of incident comms — separate, restricted, already ticketed.

Owners: Priya — fleet-b watch and re-drive. Marcus — rollback test and root cause.

---

## CUSTOMER EMAIL

**Subject:** Re: Batch submits failing / service credits — TKT-8903, TKT-8907

Hello,

Thank you for your patience, and for raising both the failures and the service-credit question. Apologies that this reply has taken longer than it should have.

**What happened.** An incident affecting Northstar's Batch API began at 11:42 UTC today, 9 November. It affected a portion of Batch API requests. Our other APIs were not affected. We applied a mitigation at 12:58 UTC and the Batch API has been recovering since. We are now in a monitoring period and are not yet treating the incident as resolved.

**Your account.** Between 11:42 and 12:58 UTC your account made 9,400 Batch API requests, of which 3,410 returned an error — approximately 36% of your Batch traffic in that window. The first failed request was at 11:43 and the last at 12:56 UTC.

**Service credits.** Schedule B of your agreement sets out how this is determined. Under B.5, Monthly Availability is calculated by Northstar from its own service records **after the end of the calendar month** to which it relates, and published within 10 business days of month end. Any credit claim is then submitted within 30 days of that publication. We are therefore not able to confirm whether the 99.9% commitment will be breached, or what credit would apply, before that determination is made. We will publish the figure on time and make sure you have what you need to assess a claim.

**Next.** We will write to you again by 15:00 UTC today with the outcome of our monitoring. In the meantime our public status page carries the current service position.

Regards,
Northstar Incident Command

---

## STATUS PAGE UPDATE

## 2026-11-09 14:20 — Monitoring

We have applied a mitigation to the incident affecting the Batch API, which began at 11:42 UTC today. Error rates on the Batch API have returned to near-normal levels. We are monitoring before we confirm recovery, and will not treat the incident as resolved until that monitoring window closes at 14:30 UTC. No other Northstar API was affected.

Correction: our 12:05 update said we had identified the cause of these errors. That was premature — the root cause has not been confirmed.

We will post another update by 15:00 UTC.

*Monitoring.*
